text.p: An earthquake shook Cyprus and the Israeli city of Tel Aviv on Monday, residents and officials said.
There were no immediate reports of casualties or damage.
The Israel Seismology Institute reported that the quake measured 6.3 on the Richter scale.
Residents of Tel Aviv said the tremor shook buildings for about 20 seconds.
Cyprus radio reported that the tremor, which lasted for about 30 seconds, was felt in the western and southern resorts of Paphos and Limassol, and to a lesser extent in capital Nicosia.
"It was quite strong," said a duty officer at police headquarters.
Tremors have been felt often on the Mediterranean island since an earthquake measuring 6.5 on the Richter scale struck on October 9, damaging some buildings.
